milestone: Brownie Runtime Release Readiness Finite Closure

strategic_capability_mapping.relationship: Turns the existing split Runtime boundary semantics into one canonical, guarded public contract and compatibility matrix for headless run, continue, inspect, event, and result flows.
Gives headless and CLI callers a stable guarded boundary for run, continue, inspect, event, and result semantics without moving scheduler or policy logic outside Runtime.
Keeps controlled tool and workspace mutation surfaces anchored to Runtime-owned protocol contracts while preserving CLI and VSIX as bounded transport/projection layers.

answers.strategic_capabilities: Advances runtime_boundary_protocol_contracts, headless_autonomous_development, and thin_cli_and_vsix_transport by making the public Runtime boundary canonical and release-guarded.
answers.new_capability: The existing Runtime release-readiness guard can now reject missing or drifting boundary surfaces, method subset, CLI/VSIX/Runtime/spec anchors, compatibility matrix entries, and non-authority language.
answers.why_existing_functionality_is_insufficie: Before RRP-1, Run Request, Runtime Event, Control Command, Run Result/Attestation, CLI external-loop, run inspection, task runtime, and VSIX validation contracts existed but were split across many docs and implementations without one guarded public inventory.
answers.product_gap_if_skipped: Brownie could ship a Runtime release with split or stale boundary semantics even while individual Rust, CLI, and VSIX checks still passed.
answers.non_duplicative: This phase adds a machine-checked canonical boundary contract and guard coverage; it is not a report-only audit, readiness wrapper, endpoint count, RPC mirror, or documentation-only verdict.
answers.no_new_rpc: Yes. RRP-1 uses existing protocol surfaces and guards; it does not add JSON-RPC methods or runtime execution paths.
answers.no_new_summary: Yes. The canonical contract is a release guard artifact, not a runtime report, digest, history, verdict, preview, or diagnostic wrapper endpoint.
answers.runtime_behavior_change: Runtime release readiness now fails closed when the canonical public boundary contract is absent, incomplete, internally inconsistent, or missing required anchors and non-authority language.
answers.headless_autonomous_contribution: Autonomous loops can rely on a guarded public boundary for run/resume/inspect/result interactions before later cancel, recovery, migration, and durability phases close their own blockers.
answers.milestone_progress: Closes the `runtime-boundary-protocol-contracts` P0 blocker while Runtime Release Ready remains false until the other recorded P0/P1 blockers are closed.

guard_engine_change_review.review_intent: RRP-1 changes the Runtime release-readiness guard and current phase manifest. Review must confirm the new canonical boundary contract is a guarded release capability, keeps CLI/VSIX transport-only, and does not claim Runtime Release Ready while other P0/P1 blockers remain open.

exit_criteria: A canonical Runtime boundary contract and compatibility matrix exists.
The Runtime release-readiness guard validates required boundary surfaces, required public method subset, CLI/VSIX/Runtime/spec anchors, compatibility matrix entries, and non-authority language.
The Runtime Release Readiness audit marks `runtime-boundary-protocol-contracts` closed and removes it from `release_ready_blocked_by`.
Runtime Release Ready remains false while the other Runtime P0/P1 blockers and owner license/publish decision remain open.

No new JSON-RPC method, scheduler, daemon, hosted platform, generic shell, arbitrary process execution, remote transport, forge adapter, signing infrastructure, package manager, registry, CLI-owned policy, or VSIX-owned policy is added.
behavior_evidence: Runtime release-readiness guard test accepts the canonical contract.
Runtime release-readiness guard tests reject missing required boundary surfaces, missing CLI/VSIX anchors, missing required method subset, and missing non-authority language.
Runtime release-readiness guard passes against repository audit and canonical boundary contract.
Runtime release-readiness audit records RRP-1 closure while keeping Runtime Release Ready false.

accepted_capability: The public Runtime boundary contract is canonical and release-guarded.
`runtime-boundary-protocol-contracts` is closed as a Runtime Release Readiness P0 blocker.
behavior_evidence: scripts/guard-runtime-release-readiness.test.mjs validates positive and negative canonical boundary contract cases.
scripts/guard-runtime-release-readiness.mjs validates docs/architecture/runtime-boundary-canonical-contract.json in the existing VSIX-invoked check path.
safety_boundary: Rust Runtime remains the execution, admission, replay, permission, tool, workspace mutation, and completion authority.
CLI and VSIX remain thin transport/projection/validation layers.
The canonical boundary contract is a narrowing release guard; it cannot grant Runtime authority or widen Mode Pack policy.
non_goals: Does not add new Runtime RPC methods.
Does not add Streamable HTTP, OAuth, MCP Apps, Sampling, Roots, Elicitation, hosted secret manager, public registry, or automatic install.

Does not add hosted scheduler, background polling, permanent daemon, worker fleet, generic shell, arbitrary process execution, hosted platform, forge/notification adapters, remote Git expansion, package installation, signing infrastructure, or remote binary distribution.
Does not reopen MCP-S1 through MCP-S7.

Does not close explicit cancel, process-loss recovery E2E, durable schema migration, full CI workflow hardening, protocol/event canonization, module decomposition, or platform/deadline/durability blockers.
rejected_alternatives: Rejected generating a broad endpoint inventory from source strings because RRP-1 needs stable release semantics, not an endpoint count.
Rejected adding a runtime status/report endpoint because release readiness should fail in CI before runtime execution.
Rejected moving schema authority into VSIX because the VSIX must remain a thin validator/projection layer.
Rejected closing protocol/event canonization in this phase because that remains a separate P1 ownership-map and drift-test blocker.
technical_debt: Remaining Runtime Release Readiness blockers: explicit cancel command, real process-loss recovery E2E, durable schema version and migration, runtime-release-guard CI workflow hardening, protocol/event canonization, runtime module decomposition reevaluation, and platform/deadline/durability hardening.
Owner license/publish decision remains required before OSS release basis can be claimed.

runtime_release_dod: Canonical Runtime public boundary contract and compatibility matrix.
Existing VSIX-invoked release-readiness guard coverage for that contract.
external_control_plane_responsibilities: Scheduling, background polling, daemons, hosted queues, worker fleets, leases, hosted isolation, metrics, alerts, SLAs, billing, and concrete Secret Provider products.
external_adapter_responsibilities: GitHub/GitLab Apps, PR workflows, Slack/Teams/email, SIEM, OTel, customer-system adapters, remote transports, registries, package distribution, and signing infrastructure.
commercial_solution_readiness: Enterprise tenant management, SSO/RBAC server, admin UI, monitoring backend, billing, SLA, private registry, and certified stack.

next_capability_rationale: After RRP-1 merge, continue to the next recorded Runtime Release Readiness P0 blocker, currently `explicit-cancel-command`.
